Agent: Hello?
Caller: Hey. This is [NAME] from [ORG].
Caller: Am I speaking with [NAME]?
Agent: [ORG], [curious] is it? Ah, you are. [curious] This is [NAME]. Who's this now?
Caller: Hey, [NAME]. I'm [NAME] with [ORG]. I'm following up on a form you submitted looking for some health insurance info. Just need to grab a few quick details to get you connected with a licensed agent.
Agent: Oh, right, the form. [uncertain] Yeah, I think I did fill out something like that, now that you mention it. Health insurance, you say? [curious] What kind of details would ya need, love?
Caller: Just the basics to get you matched up. First off, are you looking for a family plan or just an individual plan for yourself?
Agent: Ah, just for meself, love. [calm] [NAME], God rest her soul, she passed a few years back, so it's just me now.
Caller: I'm so sorry to hear that about [NAME].
Caller: So just an individual plan for you then. And how old are you, [NAME]?
Agent: Ah, she was a grand woman, she was. [nostalgic] We had some great years, you know. Ah, no bother, she's in a better place now, God love her. [calm] I'm 62, me darlin'. Born on Saint Patrick's Day, [DOB]. [chuckling] A grand day for it, that was.
Caller: That makes you sixty two then. Alright.
Caller: And what's your ZIP code?
Agent: Aye, that's right. [calm] Sixty-two. That's right, 62. [calm] And the zip code is [ZIP]. That's for Dorchester, you know, right here in Boston.
Caller: Perfect, [NAME]. Gonna put you on hold for one to two minutes while I try to connect you to an agent. Thanks.
Agent: Alright, [calm] no bother at all. I'll just hold on here.
Caller: [NAME], I have your licensed agent on the line to assist.
Caller: I'll be dropping off now.
Agent: Oh, grand! [hopeful] That was quick now. Alright, [grateful] thanks a million, [NAME]. You're a darlin'.
Caller: Hello. This is [NAME]
Caller: health insurance adviser. Are you looking for individual or family plan today?
Agent: Hello there, [NAME]. [calm] [NAME] here. Ah, hello there, [NAME]. [calm] [NAME] here. Just an individual plan for meself, now. My wife, [NAME], she passed a few years back, God rest her. So it's just me.
Caller: Starting with this individual plan, your first and last name?
Agent: [NAME], that's D-E-C-L-A-N, and O'Brien is O apostrophe B-R-I-E-N. [calm] Like the old Irish name, you know.
Caller: Got it. Alright. And your date of birth, sir?
Agent: My date of birth, now, that's [DOB]. [chuckling] A good day for a birthday, that. Saint Patrick's Day, you know.
Caller: Yes. Nice time to party and drink.
Agent: Ah, you know it! [chuckling] Many a pint was raised on my birthday, that's for sure. And many a pint I poured too, back when I managed the pub for decades. [nostalgic] Good times, good times.
Caller: Alright. And your ZIP code?
Agent: The zip code is [ZIP]. [calm] Dorchester, that is.
Caller: Yes. And your ZIP code so we can bring up all the plans, mhmm, all the plans in your region?
Agent: It's [ZIP], [calm] darlin'. That's for Dorchester, here in Boston. Is that what you needed?
Caller: Yes. Your ZIP code is correct.
Agent: Grand. [calm] So what's next, then?
Caller: Alright. And right. And now at this time, sir, are you currently insured or uninsured?
Agent: Well, that's the thing, now. [uncertain] I had a plan through me old job, running the pub, you know, but I'm mostly retired these days. So I'm a bit... uninsured, I suppose you could say. [worried] That's why I'm calling, to get that sorted.
Caller: And then also, sir, with this new health insurance plan, do you have a specific that you go to? Would you like for us to keep it open?
Agent: Ah, well, [uncertain] I used to go to [NAME], over in Southie, but I'm not set on anyone in particular, no. Keep it open, I suppose, [calm] whatever's best. As long as I can see a doctor when I need to, that's the main thing.
Caller: Okay.
Caller: Alright, sir. And at this time, are you currently taking any prescriptions?
Agent: [curious] So what do you recommend? Prescriptions, now... [thinking] Let me see. I take a little something for me blood pressure, just a small pill, you know. And sometimes for me joints, the old knees aren't what they used to be after all those years on me feet behind the bar. [calm] Nothing major, though.
Caller: Okay. Got it.
Agent: So, [curious] what's the craic now? What kinda plans are we talkin' about?
Caller: Alright. And And what's what did you say, sir? Your microphone went in and out?
Agent: Oh, [calm] I just said, "What's the craic?" It's an Irish saying, you know. Means "What's happening?" or "What's next?" [chuckling] Just wondering what we do now.
Caller: Oh, oh, okay. I do have to ask you these questions to get you the accurate correct plan. That will be for you, sir.
Agent: Ah, no, [calm] no bother at all, me boy. I understand. Just me being a bit chatty, you know. Go right ahead. Ask away.

Agent: Right, well, [uncertain] I'm mostly retired, you know. I get a bit from me pension, and some savings. I'd say... maybe around twenty-five thousand, give or take. [nervous] Is that too much?
